title: USB Type-C port controller (DRP): CC1 / CC2 attach detection with a 100-clock debounce and orientation, 10-clock detach, source / sink role, VBUS enable, CC fault detection, and an 8 x 8-bit register file

words.name: CC_STATUS
words.desc: {attached, orientation, fsm[1:0], cc2[1:0], cc1[1:0]} (fsm: 0 unattached, 1 attach wait, 2 attached)

words.name: ROLE_CTRL
words.desc: bit 0: 1 = source / DFP (reset), 0 = sink / UFP; vbus_en needs the source role

words.name: FAULT_STAT
words.desc: bit 0: abnormal CC level seen (sticky, write 1 to clear; a fault in the same clock wins)

words.name: INT_STAT
words.desc: bit 0 attach, bit 1 detach, bit 2 fault (sticky, write 1 to clear; a new event in the same clock wins)

words.name: ORIENT
words.desc: bit 0: orientation (1 = CC2 is the wired CC)

irqs.name: EVENT
irqs.desc: an abnormal CC level is present or an INT_STAT bit is set; held while either lasts, so the bit is set again on every clock until INT_STAT is cleared and the fault is gone

notes: cc1 / cc2 (2-bit CC line levels: 0 open, 1 Rd, 2 Ra, 3 abnormal), attached, orientation and vbus_en pass through unchanged.
The core's 8-bit register file is mapped one register per word (bits 7:0); a write with PSTRB != 4'hF is dropped with PSLVERR.
